bugs.explanation: Heading levels should not skip. Jumping from `<h1>` to `<h3>` leaves a gap in the document outline, which confuses screen readers and harms SEO. Use `<h2>` as the next level after `<h1>`.

title: Link Opens New Tab Without noopener

bugs.explanation: Opening a link in a new tab with `target="_blank"` exposes the current page to a vulnerability called reverse tabnapping — the new tab can access `window.opener` and redirect the original page. Add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to prevent this.

A `<button>` without a `type` attribute inside a `<form>` defaults to `type="submit"`, which submits the form on click. This is often the desired behavior, but it should be explicit. Use `type="submit"` for submit buttons, `type="button"` for JS-triggered buttons, and `type="reset"` for reset buttons.

title: input Placeholder Is Not a Label

bugs.fix:
<label for="name">Your name</label>
<input type="text" id="name" placeholder="e.g. Alice">
bugs.explanation: Placeholder text disappears when the user starts typing and is not announced reliably by screen readers. Never use placeholder as a substitute for a `<label>`. Provide a proper `<label>` element and optionally use placeholder for an example value.

title: Form Radio Group Missing name
code:
<input type="radio" value="yes"> Yes
<input type="radio" value="no"> No

bugs.explanation: Radio buttons with no `name` attribute belong to no group — they can all be selected simultaneously. The `name` attribute groups related radio buttons so only one can be selected at a time.

title: Anchor Without href Is Not a Link

bugs.explanation: An `<a>` tag without `href` is not an interactive link — it isn't focusable by keyboard and isn't announced as a link by screen readers. Either add an `href` or use a `<button>` if the action is purely JavaScript-driven.

Block-level elements like `<div>` cannot be nested inside inline elements like `<span>`. This is invalid HTML — browsers will attempt to repair the DOM but may produce unexpected rendering. Use a block element (`<div>`) as the outer container.

Browsers will automatically insert `<tbody>` even when missing, which can break CSS selectors and cause unexpected layout. Explicitly use `<thead>` for header rows and `<tbody>` for data rows for correct semantics and predictable styling.

title: required Attribute on Checkbox
code:
<input type="checkbox" name="agree" required>
<label>I agree to the terms</label>

bugs.explanation: Without a blank placeholder option, the first real option is pre-selected when the form loads. Users who haven't actively chosen 'USA' might submit it accidentally. Add an empty placeholder option so users must make a deliberate selection.

title: nav Without aria-label When Multiple navs

bugs.explanation: When a page has multiple `<nav>` elements, screen readers announce them all as 'navigation'. Users can't distinguish between them. Add `aria-label` to each to provide meaningful names: `aria-label="Main navigation"` and `aria-label="Footer navigation"`.
